why: Mule-deer same-animal phenological phase is strongly entangled with departure DOY; an independent radar and local land-surface-phenology panel may separate ecological date responses at station-year resolution.

original_article.title: Shifts in avian migration phenologies do not compensate for changes to conditions en route in spring and fall

source_origin: NOAA weather surveillance radar bird-passage measures, MODIS vegetation metrics, NARR temperature/humidity, NOT eBird; individual bird tracks do NOT exist in these source summaries
registered_focal_questions: Does independent radar passage phenology contain additional association with vegetation greenup after adjusting for concurrent climate and site/calendar structure?
Do held-out YEAR predictions benefit from green-up beyond predeclared date/climate baseline?
prior_art: The 2025 Adams article already reports stronger temperature responses than greenup, incomplete climate compensation and weather-radar passage trends. Replicating those headline results is not PAYOFF novelty.
tentative_identification: station-year group passage calendar date and station-year vegetation greenup share temporal structures. Their station/year/environment residual covariation must be assessed BEFORE any new coefficient. Radar assemblage passage is not a bird's decision-time cue or fitness.
pending_model: If original row-grain and positive identifying residual variation pass, predeclare blocked held-out-year predictive comparison with explicit full covariates before fitting any candidate effect. Do not fit source author's published coefficient opportunistically.
upstream_constraint: Never use eBird, TinyFish, posttarget cue values as predecision information, original unverified raw bird IDs, or optimize thresholds after observing outcome.
output: Aggregate-only source inventory including file MD5 if present, file sizes, classifiable columns, and explicit decision on suitability for a further new preregistered model.
